newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks get lift in morning from Wall St rise.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks get lift in morning from Wall St rise.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks inched ahead on Tuesday morning as an overnight rise on Wall Street gave prices a lift, but brokers said a lack of domestic news would limit the rise and investors were awaiting corporate results.
"The rise in the overseas U.S. market triggered today's rise but a lot of people are staying on the sidelines to see what happens next week," said Ricky Tam, research manger at Delta Asia Securities.
The Hang Seng Index was up 20.07 points, or 0.15 percent, at 13,395.76 after rising to a morning high of 13,453.73. Turnover was HK$2.17 billion after the first 45 minutes of trade.
HSBC Holdings is due to release its 1996 results on Monday. The stock rose HK$2.00 to HK$190.50.

Analysts said investors were also awaiting U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on Wednesday and some overseas investors remained cautious about the situation in China following the death last week of Deng Xiaoping. Funeral rites were taking place for the deceased patriarch in Beijing on Tuesday morning.
"When they see the situation in China, they are a bit more careful before they jump in," Tam said.
He said local investors were less worried about instability. "Deng transferred his power to (Chinese president) Jiang Zemin a long time ago," he said.

H-shares extended Monday's strong gains with a rise of 10.33 points, or 1.06 percent, in the Hang Seng China Enterprises Index, to 984.24. Among the H-share index components, Shandong Xinhua surged HK$0.15, or 6.52 percent, to HK$2.45.
"People feel they are looking at economic recovery in China and fundamentally a sector in the market that has promises to offer," said one trader.
China Eastern Airlines fell HK$0.02 to HK$1.61 after rising HK$0.22 on Monday.
Shares in New World Infrastructure rose HK$0.40 to HK$22.70. The company said it would buy a 9.9 percent stake in H-share listing candidate Beijing Datang Power Generation Co.

Property stocks were mixed on Tuesday. New World Development rose HK$0.20 to HK$48.50 and Cheung Kong advanced HK$0.25 to HK$72.00 but Sun Hung Kai Properties fell HK$0.25 to HK$89.25 and Henderson Land slipped HK$0.25 to HK$69.25.
The Dow industrials rose 76.58 points on Monday to close at 7,008.20.
